sample_unit: cases (1055 group A, 721 group B, 144 group C, 161 group D)

links.outcome: Physician treatment decision accuracy with versus without LLM support
links.effect: LLM support increased treatment decision accuracy from 73.1% to 88.6% (odds ratio 2.86, 95% CI, 2.27-3.60; P<.001); TOAST classification odds ratio 3.63.
links.quote: In the prospective physician study, LLM support increased treatment decision accuracy from 73.1% to 88.6% (odds ratio 2.86, 95% CI, 2.27-3.60; P<.001).

links.outcome: Physician decision accuracy with and without LLM support in workflow
links.effect: Accuracy rose from 73.1% to 88.6% with LLM support; gains largest among junior and nonspecialist physicians (e.g., junior nonspecialists 0.600 to 0.846).
links.quote: Accuracy gains were largest among junior and nonspecialist physicians, including junior specialists (0.667 to 0.833), junior nonspecialists (0.600 to 0.846), and senior nonspecialists (0.667 to 0.850).

links.outcome: Hallucination and omission rates and safety scores with guideline-based multiagent framework
links.effect: Mean clinical safety score rose from 3.70 to 4.01; hallucination rate fell from 33.6% to 20.6% and omission rate from 38.5% to 24.5%.
links.quote: Across evaluated models, the multiagent framework increased the mean clinical safety score from 3.70 to 4.01 and reduced mean hallucination and omission rates from 33.6% to 20.6% and from 38.5% to 24.5%, respectively.

links.outcome: Treatment recommendation accuracy of multiagent framework versus baseline LLMs on same cases
links.effect: Model-level accuracy ranges increased from 0.546-0.737 to 0.687-0.851 in group A, 0.587-0.698 to 0.671-0.813 in group B, and 0.507-0.646 to 0.667-0.750 in group C.
links.quote: Model-level accuracy ranges increased from 0.546-0.737 to 0.687-0.851 in group A, from 0.587-0.698 to 0.671-0.813 in group B, and from 0.507-0.646 to 0.667-0.750 in group C.

unlisted_practices: Multiagent LLM framework with structured outputs and guideline-based reasoning to improve accuracy

screen.reason: The study develops and validates a novel multiagent LLM framework for stroke treatment decision support, evaluating its benchmark performance and its impact on clinician decisions in a prospective reader study (offline vignettes/cases). Developing a multiagent architecture is AI system development rather than testing a health care deployment practice/safeguard.
